55:7.en: And the sky He hath uplifted; and He hath set the measure

55:8.en: That ye exceed not the measure

55:9.ar: وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلۡوَزۡنَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ وَلَا تُخۡسِرُواْ ٱلۡمِيزَانَ
55:9.en: But observe the measure strictly, nor fall short thereof

2:143.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَسَطࣰ ا لِّتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدࣰ اۗ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡقِبۡلَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيۡهَآ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِۚ وَإِن كَانَتۡ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَٰنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:143.en: Thus We have appointed you a middle nation, that ye may be witnesses against mankind, and that the messenger may be a witness against you. And We appointed the qiblah which ye formerly observed only that We might know him who followeth the messenger, from him who turneth on his heels. In truth it was a hard (test) save for those whom Allah guided. But it was not Allah's purpose that your faith should be in vain, for Allah is Full of Pity, Merciful toward mankind

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

51:56.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡتُ ٱلۡجِنَّ وَٱلۡإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُونِ
51:56.en: I created the jinn and humankind only that they might worship Me

17:1.ar: سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَسۡرَىٰ بِعَبۡدِهِۦ لَيۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِ إِلَى ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡأَقۡصَا ٱلَّذِي بَٰرَكۡنَا حَوۡلَهُۥ لِنُرِيَهُۥ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَآۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡبَصِيرُ
17:1.en: Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far distant place of worship the neighbourhood whereof We have blessed, that We might show him of Our tokens! Lo! He, only He, is the Hearer, the Seer

klFVf7b4Nms.speaker: adnan
klFVf7b4Nms.speaker_note: 17th and final part of his 'Achieving the Balance' series, recaps his earlier khutbahs and speaks of his own childhood
klFVf7b4Nms.title: Achieving the Balance: Stewardship and Service
klFVf7b4Nms.one_line: Series finale: after recapping sixteen balances, he argues the foundational one is being both Allah's steward (khalifa) and His servant (abd).
klFVf7b4Nms.summary: Closing his Achieving the Balance series, he returns to the verses on the mizan in Surah Ar-Rahman: nothing in life functions without balance, and both extremes of the pendulum make Islam harm rather than serve you. Muslims were made a nation of moderation, and deviation grows from losing this balance, so before pushing an agenda one should check one's approach, since Islam belongs to Allah and people must fit it rather than make it fit them. He recaps the sixteen balances he has covered, from integration with identity to effort with reliance. In the second khutbah he explains why the series exists: he has watched too many rational young people leave Islam after being taught an unbalanced version. The most important balance is who you are: a khalifa, responsible for fixing what is broken and caring for everyone's wellbeing, and an abd, a servant without ego or agenda. Stewardship without servanthood produces tyrants; servanthood without stewardship produces passive, oppressed people. Real responsibility means sustained activism, not a week of outrage over Palestine. Moderation is not indecision. He ends with the Prophet calling himself the most servant of servants when mocked for eating like a slave.

outline.heading: Opening
The mizan in Surah Ar-Rahman
outline.gist: The whole series comes back to two verses: Allah raised the heavens and set the balance, so do not transgress it. He stresses that this is balance itself, not merely scales.

outline.heading: Without balance nothing works
outline.gist: The word mizan is repeated three times in a surah that does nothing but count blessings. An unbalanced life is not a happy one, and balance governs mental, social, financial and physical life, the poor, the sick and the planet.

outline.heading: Either extreme makes Islam fail you
outline.gist: The pendulum swings hard in both directions; whoever sits at an extreme finds that Islam no longer serves them, and they harm themselves and others.

outline.heading: A nation of moderation
outline.gist: In the middle of the qiblah passage Allah says He made you a middle nation, witnesses over people with the Prophet as your example. Life is not either-or: you can hold to the authentic and still take a new approach, and deviation and bid'ah grow from losing this balance.

outline.heading: Before you push an agenda, check your balance
outline.gist: Before forming an unchallengeable opinion or being fiercely for or against something, ask whether your approach is balanced. Islam belongs to Allah, not to him or to you.

outline.heading: Recap: integration with identity
outline.gist: You cannot make Islam fit you; you fit Islam. Over sixteen weeks he first covered integrating and living with any society while holding on to your identity.

outline.heading: Recap: peace, gender roles, power
outline.gist: Advocating peace while refusing oppression and intellectual tyranny; men and women as partners, not at war; and last week, accepting a man's responsibility without abusing its power.

outline.heading: Recap: heart and mind, effort and results
outline.gist: Balancing the essence and mechanics of worship, the heart and the mind in faith, and full effort with leaving the results to Allah.

outline.heading: Recap: dua answered on His terms
outline.gist: Allah responds, but not necessarily with what you want when you want it. Small misunderstandings like this are a glitch in the code that later blows up; Allah is omnipotent and we do our job without questioning Him.

outline.heading: Recap: wisdom, wealth, the unseen
outline.gist: Seeking wisdom while submitting when it is not clear; earning as much as possible while living with asceticism; and believing in the unseen without superstition.

outline.heading: Hold the pendulum in the middle
outline.gist: Superstitious abuse is cultural, not Islamic. Without willingness to think, weigh evidence and hear other views, your pendulum swings; the aim is to hold it in the middle. This is the final piece of the series.

outline.heading: The most important balance: who you are
outline.gist: As a child he struggled to see the point of all the worship until his teachers explained his role and his coordinates; understand this and everything else follows.

outline.heading: Interlude
Why young people walk away
outline.gist: He has watched too many young people leave Islam because the parents or teachers who taught them were too conservative or too loose. Young people see without cultural lenses, spot the imbalance and leave; the responsibility lies with those who taught them.

outline.heading: When they reach him it is too late
outline.gist: By the time parents bring a child who has decided to leave, the child sees him as apologetic. He insists nothing he says from the minbar is apologetic or said under pressure.

outline.heading: Our problems are homemade
outline.gist: He is pressured by no one, Muslim or not, and believes Muslims in this country have nothing to hide. The problems are of our own making.

outline.heading: Every creature knows its role but us
outline.gist: Insects, birds and the tuna that returns to where it was born all know what they are here to do. Humans do not, so we need revelation to tell us who we are.

outline.heading: Two coordinates: khalifa and abd
outline.gist: You are a steward and a servant; drop one and you become something you were not designed to be, inflate one and you walk with a limp. Allah said He would place a khalifa on earth: the first coordinate.

outline.heading: The steward: responsible for everyone's wellbeing
outline.gist: The second coordinate is that you are here only to serve. As a steward you are accountable for others' destinies: see something broken and fix it, see a gap and fill it.

outline.heading: Stewardship without service becomes tyranny
outline.gist: Responsibility must be carried out as service to Allah, not control. Drop service and the steward turns into a tyrant who wants to coerce everyone; ask whether Allah would approve of what you say.

outline.heading: Service without stewardship becomes weakness
outline.gist: Servants have no egos, agendas or need to own. But a servant who feels no responsibility becomes passive, disconnected and oppressed, until even his religion is taken from him; humility and love must go with initiative.

outline.heading: Both together, never either-or
outline.gist: Everything Allah made has a description, and yours is steward and servant together. Start there and every other part of Islam falls into place; one who knows he is a servant never oppresses anyone.

outline.heading: A week of outrage is not responsibility
outline.gist: A responsible person stays with a problem until it is fixed. Instead we get excited for a week over Palestine or an offensive poster, then forget. Are you fulfilling both roles, or waiting for others?

outline.heading: Problems that last twenty years
outline.gist: Problems persist for decades only because we have not grasped that we are servants and stewards; someone who sees a problem will not look away until it is addressed with time, wealth, expertise or advocacy.

outline.heading: Moderation is not indecision: what is your part?
outline.gist: Being the middle nation means being decisive once the balance is set. His job is to feel responsible for your faith and serve you, not control you, and to be removed if he fails; what are you doing for the ummah?

outline.heading: His servant: the highest accolade
outline.gist: This is what the companions learned in ten years in Makkah: when Allah elevated the Prophet He called him His servant, the highest honour anyone can reach.

outline.heading: The servant of servants
outline.gist: Seen eating with poor people, knee to his chest, he was mocked as eating like a slave and answered that no one is more of a servant than he. He also carried full responsibility: the perfect combination.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Moderation and balance (wasatiyyah)
themes.note: The mizan governs every area of life; the middle nation avoids both extremes, and the series' sixteen balances illustrate it.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Young people leave Islam when taught an unbalanced version that fails their rational scrutiny; blame lies with the teachers.

themes.label: Extremism, bad religiosity and distorted practice
themes.note: Overly conservative or overly loose teaching from parents or teachers pushes people away from Allah.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Humans need revelation to know their role: steward responsible for the world and servant of Allah, held in balance.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Servants have no ego, agenda or need to own; this keeps stewardship from becoming tyranny.

themes.label: Activism, civic engagement and the path forward
themes.note: Responsibility means staying with a problem until it is solved, not brief outrage; each person must name their contribution to the ummah.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: The Prophet embraced servanthood when mocked while carrying full responsibility: the perfect combination.

quran.point: Allah established the balance and forbade transgressing it: the anchor of the whole series.
We made you a middle nation to be witnesses over people, with the Prophet as your example.
Allah places a khalifa on earth: the first coordinate of who you are.
You are only here to serve Allah: the second coordinate.
When Allah honours the Prophet He calls him His servant.

hadith.gist: A woman mocked the Prophet for eating like a slave as he sat with poor people; he replied that no one is more of a servant than he.

maxims: An unbalanced life is not a happy one
You can't make Islam fit you; you fit Islam
Islam belongs to Allah, not to me or you
You are an abd and a khalifa
Servants don't have egos
Our problems are homemade

stories.point: He struggled with the point of worship until teachers explained his role; understanding it made everything fit.

stories.who: Young people brought to him too late

stories.who: The Prophet mocked as eating like a slave
stories.point: Being a servant is the highest honour, and he paired it with full responsibility.

contemporary: Muslims' short-lived outrage over Palestine and an offensive poster, followed by forgetting
He insists he speaks without pressure from Muslims, non-Muslims or the country, and that Muslims in Canada have nothing to hide
takeaways: Check that your approach is balanced before forming fixed opinions or pushing an agenda
See yourself as both steward and servant: take responsibility without ego or control
When you see a problem, keep working on it until it is fixed rather than reacting for a week
Teach young people a balanced Islam that holds up to rational questions
Ask yourself what your own contribution to the ummah is

57:1.ar: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
57:1.en: All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifieth Allah; and He is the Mighty, the Wise

57:2.ar: لَهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
57:2.en: His is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth; He quickeneth and He giveth death; and He is Able to do all things

57:3.ar: هُوَ ٱلۡأَوَّلُ وَٱلۡأٓخِرُ وَٱلظَّٰهِرُ وَٱلۡبَاطِنُۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ
57:3.en: He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward; and He is Knower of all things

57:4.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ يَعۡلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡهَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعۡرُجُ فِيهَاۖ وَهُوَ مَعَكُمۡ أَيۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرࣱ‏
57:4.en: He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days; then He mounted the Throne. He knoweth all that entereth the earth and all that emergeth therefrom and all that cometh down from the sky and all that ascendeth therein; and He is with you wheresoever ye may be. And Allah is Seer of what ye do

57:5.ar: لَّهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
57:5.en: His is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth, and unto Allah (all) things are brought back

57:6.ar: يُولِجُ ٱلَّيۡلَ فِي ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِي ٱلَّيۡلِۚ وَهُوَ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
57:6.en: He causeth the night to pass into the day, and He causeth the day to pass into the night, and He is knower of all that is in the breasts

9:40.ar: إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدۡ نَصَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ثَانِيَ ٱثۡنَيۡنِ إِذۡ هُمَا فِي ٱلۡغَارِ إِذۡ يَقُولُ لِصَٰحِبِهِۦ لَا تَحۡزَنۡ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَاۖ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَيَّدَهُۥ بِجُنُودࣲ لَّمۡ تَرَوۡهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ ٱلسُّفۡلَىٰۗ وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِيَ ٱلۡعُلۡيَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
9:40.en: If ye help him not, still Allah helped him when those who disbelieve drove him forth, the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us. Then Allah caused His peace of reassurance to descend upon him and supported him with hosts ye cannot see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the nethermost, while Allah's Word it was that became the uppermost. Allah is Mighty, Wise

15:29.ar: فَإِذَا سَوَّيۡتُهُۥ وَنَفَخۡتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِي فَقَعُواْ لَهُۥ سَٰجِدِينَ
15:29.en: So, when I have made him and have breathed into him of My Spirit, do ye fall down, prostrating yourselves unto him

17:85.ar: وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلرُّوحِۖ قُلِ ٱلرُّوحُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِ رَبِّي وَمَآ أُوتِيتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
17:85.en: They are asking thee concerning the Spirit. Say: The Spirit is by command of my Lord, and of knowledge ye have been vouchsafed but little

2kyvc1tdyNg.speaker: adnan
2kyvc1tdyNg.speaker_note: his own Sunday tafseer series; shares a clinical experience from his medical practice
2kyvc1tdyNg.title: Sunday Tafseer: Surat Al-Hadid, Part 1 (Verses 1-3)
2kyvc1tdyNg.one_line: Al-Hadid opens by describing Allah through apparent opposites, preparing us to balance the spiritual and material sides of ourselves.
2kyvc1tdyNg.summary: He introduces Al-Hadid as the last surah of the Qaf to Hadid cluster: earlier surahs posed either-or choices, while Hadid asks us to hold together two things that seem opposite, the spiritual and the material. He warns that today's world is consumed by materialism, consuming without brakes and burning the planet's lungs. The first verses describe Allah through seeming conundrums. Tasbih means declaring Allah flawless and beyond scrutiny, the core difference between a Muslim and others; Allah questions us, not the reverse. Al-Aziz is the unfathomable, His essence the only thing we are told we will never grasp, and the human self keeps trying to bring God down to manageable size, as in superhero fantasies and gods who quarrel. Al-Hakim means we do not claim superior wisdom: after the earthquakes, the Muslim answer to unanswerable questions is Subhan Allah, then relieving pain. He recalls telling a non-smoking marathon runner he had stage four lung cancer, and says faith must work in such moments. He explains sovereignty over cosmos and our small lives, why death gives life meaning, and how being First and Last, Apparent and Hidden shows Allah is beyond time and space. He closes by urging people to revive their starved spiritual side, citing companions absorbed in prayer.

outline.heading: Recap: the Qaf to Waqi'ah cluster as a series of choices
outline.gist: Righteousness or falsehood, purpose, guidance, certainty, gratitude for blessings, and which group you will be in.

outline.heading: Hadid's curveball: two seeming opposites held together
outline.gist: Unlike the either-or surahs, Hadid asks you to harness spirituality and materialism together.

outline.heading: Why the surah is named Iron
outline.gist: Iron is where humanity's material civilization began, yet the surah holds one of the Quran's most profound references to spirituality.

outline.heading: The opening verses describe Allah through apparent opposites
outline.gist: His teachers had him recite verses one to six daily; they show Allah is beyond what our minds imagine.

outline.heading: Neither purely spiritual nor purely material
outline.gist: Exclusive spirituality brings weakness and failure; exclusive materialism brings what we suffer today.

outline.heading: A world consuming without brakes
outline.gist: Global consumerism ignores warnings of a heating planet, and burning forests destroys what looks like the earth's lungs.

outline.heading: Interlude
No earlier surah of the cluster describes Allah like this
outline.gist: Others name Him or His bounties in a verse; Hadid gives six verses of description.

outline.heading: Interlude
Everything in the heavens and earth exalts Allah
outline.gist: Not repeating 'what is in' sets the heavens and the earth as two contrasting creations.

outline.heading: Al-Aziz: the unfathomable
outline.gist: If you could encompass Allah with your mind He would not be God; questions about what He is made of have no answer.

outline.heading: Only Allah's essence is beyond comprehension
outline.gist: Everything else in the deen can be understood as you study; the essence of God cannot.

outline.heading: Tasbih: Allah is flawless and not on trial
outline.gist: Declaring Allah beyond criticism is the main difference between a Muslim and a non-Muslim, which is why we say Subhan Allah in sujud.

outline.heading: He questions us; we do not question Him
outline.gist: Our opinion of what Allah does carries no weight; He never needed our counsel.

outline.heading: Heavens and earth: our small world of simple needs
outline.gist: Even the most powerful people want the same basics: food, sleep without pain, safety, health and happy relationships.

outline.heading: How creation exalts Allah
outline.gist: Stars and animals exalt Him by fulfilling the purpose they were made for; our task is to find what our tasbih looks like.

outline.heading: Why people humanize God
outline.gist: The self dislikes servanthood, so it imagines superheroes or makes God flesh, gives Him family or many quarrelling gods.

outline.heading: Tawhid offers no leverage to exploit
outline.gist: You cannot make money or control people with pure tawhid, which is why some resist it.

outline.heading: Al-Hakim: do not claim superior wisdom
outline.gist: Once you say God could have done better, you have levelled the field.

outline.heading: After the earthquakes: Subhan Allah, then do your job
outline.gist: We do not invent explanations for suffering; we exalt Allah and work to relieve pain.

outline.heading: You will face what you cannot explain
outline.gist: Being a good Muslim is easy when life is easy; Islam's tools are for hard times.

outline.heading: Telling a marathon runner he had lung cancer
outline.gist: A healthy non-smoker on anti-smoking posters received a stage four diagnosis; there was no rational answer to why.

outline.heading: Nothing personal: deal with it and move on
outline.gist: Good and bad come in Allah's large scheme; your value does not change, and the questions wait for the One who has the answers.

outline.heading: Interlude
Sovereignty over the cosmos and over our small lives
outline.gist: His dominion spans the near-infinite universe and every detail of one person's life.

outline.heading: He gives life and death
outline.gist: Not two gods in conflict as in mythology; life and death are two sides of one coin.

outline.heading: Without death there is no meaning
outline.gist: Every book imagining human immortality ends with people wanting to die; death also preserves the chance to repent.

outline.heading: Owned, not owner
outline.gist: My body and spirit belong to Allah, lent to me for a short time.

outline.heading: Omnipotent: and the meaningless questions
outline.gist: Asking whether He can create what He cannot control is playing with words, not philosophy.

outline.heading: The First and the Last: beyond time
outline.gist: First and last only exist within time; we cannot imagine anything without beginning or end.

outline.heading: If God were contained by time, time would be god
outline.gist: Allah created time; asking what came before Him has no meaning.

outline.heading: The atheist's eternal universe
outline.gist: Claiming the universe never began or ends just makes space-time a god, without evidence, since everything in it begins and ends.

outline.heading: The Apparent and the Hidden: beyond space
outline.gist: In three dimensions a thing is either seen or concealed; asking where God is assumes space contains Him.

outline.heading: The All-Knowing: what we lack is knowledge

outline.heading: Recite and reflect on the first six verses this week

outline.heading: Apparent opposites in us: spirit and matter
outline.gist: Today the material side is inflated and the spiritual starved, so people pray and feel nothing; some also go too far into spirituality.

outline.heading: The Prophet balanced both effortlessly
outline.gist: His and his companions' balance has not been seen since, and it carried Islam across the world.

outline.heading: Is your prayer mechanical? The man whose wall fell

4:34.ar: ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٰمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ وَبِمَآ أَنفَقُواْ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡۚ فَٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ قَٰنِتَٰتٌ حَٰفِظَٰتࣱ لِّلۡغَيۡبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَٱلَّٰتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَٱهۡجُرُوهُنَّ فِي ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ وَٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّۖ فَإِنۡ أَطَعۡنَكُمۡ فَلَا تَبۡغُواْ عَلَيۡهِنَّ سَبِيلًاۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيࣰّ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
4:34.en: Men are in charge of women, because Allah hath made the one of them to excel the other, and because they spend of their property (for the support of women). So good women are the obedient, guarding in secret that which Allah hath guarded. As for those from whom ye fear rebellion, admonish them and banish them to beds apart, and scourge them. Then if they obey you, seek not a way against them. Lo! Allah is ever High, Exalted, Great

4:19.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَرِثُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرۡهࣰ اۖ وَلَا تَعۡضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذۡهَبُواْ بِبَعۡضِ مَآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةࣲ مُّبَيِّنَةࣲۚ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۚ فَإِن كَرِهۡتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكۡرَهُواْ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَيَجۡعَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيۡرࣰ ا كَثِيرࣰ ا
4:19.en: O ye who believe! It is not lawful for you forcibly to inherit the women (of your deceased kinsmen), nor (that) ye should put constraint upon them that ye may take away a part of that which ye have given them, unless they be guilty of flagrant lewdness. But consort with them in kindness, for if ye hate them it may happen that ye hate a thing wherein Allah hath placed much good

38:44.ar: وَخُذۡ بِيَدِكَ ضِغۡثࣰ ا فَٱضۡرِب بِّهِۦ وَلَا تَحۡنَثۡۗ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَٰهُ صَابِرࣰ اۚ نِّعۡمَ ٱلۡعَبۡدُ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابࣱ‏
38:44.en: And (it was said unto him): Take in thine hand a branch and smite therewith, and break not thine oath. Lo! We found him steadfast, how excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (to his Lord)

18kV_TeI7HQ.speaker: adnan
18kV_TeI7HQ.speaker_note: 16th in his 'Achieving the Balance' series, mentions his ten years in the community and the Council of Imams' citywide topic
18kV_TeI7HQ.title: Achieving the Balance: Between Leadership and Abuse of Power
18kV_TeI7HQ.one_line: Citywide domestic-violence khutbah: qawwamah means caregiving responsibility, not control or ownership, and Islam allows zero abuse in the home.
18kV_TeI7HQ.summary: Part of a Council of Imams initiative on domestic violence, this sixteenth balance khutbah holds that men's qawwamah is real and non-negotiable: a man is a caregiver accountable for his household, as in the hadith that everyone is a caregiver responsible for those in their charge. The problem is confusing leadership with control; you do not own your wife, children or staff, because only Allah controls. Caregiving without control is the steward-servant balance. He reports that disclosures of abuse have risen sharply during his ten years in the city. He then shows the Prophet never struck anyone outside battle, defined the best people as the best to their wives, did housework, and used his last words to urge good treatment of women. The verse on living with wives in kindness applies even when a man dislikes his wife, and the verse often misused to justify hitting addresses a marriage collapsing from disloyalty, symbolized by Ayyub's bundle of grass, never a licence for abuse. He gives five points: raise awareness, learn the signs, refer cases to qualified helpers instead of intervening personally, recognize that children suffer most, and protect families as the cornerstone of the ummah. He closes with the Prophet shielding Aisha from Abu Bakr.

outline.heading: Opening
A citywide khutbah; every topic has a balance
outline.gist: The Council of Imams set domestic violence as the topic across the city's major centres. He fits it into his series, since every part of Islamic practice is subject to balance.

outline.heading: Qawwamah: responsible and accountable
outline.gist: Men are qawwam: put in charge, responsible and accountable for the family Allah entrusted to them. The root means establishing something and seeing it through, not expecting it to fall into place on its own.

outline.heading: Each of you is a caregiver
outline.gist: Ra'i means caregiver and sponsor, not merely shepherd. The hadith names the man as caregiver of his household: once married, his time, wealth and energy are there to serve them.

outline.heading: Leadership is not ownership
outline.gist: People confuse responsibility with control. You own a company, but not your wife, children, students, staff or clinic team; only Allah controls and coerces to His will.

outline.heading: Steward and servant together
outline.gist: Caregiving without control is the balance: a servant who feels no responsibility is weak and lets things crumble, while a steward who forgets he serves becomes a control freak.

outline.heading: Abuse has risen over ten years
outline.gist: He is not qualified to counsel marriages, yet people bring their troubles to imams, and in his ten years in the city he has heard more and more of domestic abuse.

outline.heading: Raise sons to be qawwam without abusing power
outline.gist: Do not drop qawwamah, since it is Quranic; teach boys to be responsible leaders and caregivers while making clear it never permits control or abuse of a power differential.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet never struck anyone
outline.gist: Muslims have misunderstood and mispracticed this. The Prophet never raised his hand against a woman, child or servant, only against an enemy in battle.

outline.heading: The best of you are best to their wives
outline.gist: 'Ahl' in the hadith means the wife and her descendants, not parents: the best of you are the best to their spouses, and he was the best to his.

outline.heading: The Prophet at work in his home
outline.gist: When not teaching or striving, he was at home cleaning, mending his clothes, repairing shoes and caring for his family.

outline.heading: His final bequest: treat women well
outline.gist: Three days before his death, too sick to walk, he was carried to the minbar and bequeathed that women be treated with the best you have.

outline.heading: Farewell sermon: you own nothing of them
outline.gist: Wives are your helpers and supporters; you own nothing of them. You took them by Allah's word and covenant and will answer to that covenant.

outline.heading: Live with them in kindness, even in dislike
outline.gist: The verse that you may dislike something in which Allah places much good is quoted for everything except marriage, its real context. A man who says he does not connect with his wife is looking for a way out.

outline.heading: Islam allows zero abuse
outline.gist: She is your wife by Allah's covenant: take care of her. A wife who shows a qadi any sign of physical harm sees her husband jailed, and the verse people cite is no green card to beat anyone.

outline.heading: The verse on a failing marriage and Ayyub's grass
outline.gist: The passage addresses a marriage collapsing from disloyalty: tender advice, then leaving the room, then a gesture like Ayyub's bundle of grass that signals the end. Nowhere may a man shout at, insult or demean his wife.

outline.heading: His teacher: go home and work it out
outline.gist: A year into his marriage, a student complained about his wife to their sheikh, who told him to go home and sort it out because he was lucky to have a wife who shared his values.

outline.heading: No balance for abuse
outline.gist: Verbal, emotional, financial and physical abuse are all unacceptable, with no middle ground. You will be asked whether you cared for the one in your keeping, and you would never accept abuse for your daughter, mother or sister.

outline.heading: Point one: raise awareness
outline.gist: Domestic violence exists in every society, ours included; he speaks to his own community, where nearly everyone knows of at least one abusive relationship.

outline.heading: Point two: know the signs
outline.gist: Victims rarely come forward because family, children and future are at stake, so friends must learn to read the signs.

outline.heading: Point three: refer to qualified help
outline.gist: Help means bringing the case to professionals such as government services or the MRC, not ruining a family or making it a personal vendetta; untrained intervention makes things worse and ignores people's autonomy.

outline.heading: Point four: children suffer most
outline.gist: Children hide their pain but carry it for decades into their relationships. Putting up with abuse 'for their sake' subjects them to trauma; he can spot a traumatized child within half an hour.

outline.heading: Point five: families are the cornerstone of the ummah
outline.gist: The ummah is collective families; when families fail there is no ummah. Remove every trace of abuse, seek help, and remember you are qawwam to serve, not to coerce.

outline.heading: Ninety percent of the job happens at home
outline.gist: Institutions can hardly teach youth from broken or abusive homes. How you treat your wife is how your son will treat his; masjids add only the remaining ten percent.

outline.heading: The five points in sum
outline.gist: Spread awareness, know the signs, reach out for help without stepping into what you cannot handle, remember the children, and invest in families or bargain away the future.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet shields Aisha from Abu Bakr
outline.gist: Hearing Aisha raise her voice at the Prophet, Abu Bakr came to rebuke her; the Prophet kept stepping between them, then joked that he had defended her, and Abu Bakr asked to enter now that there was peace.

outline.heading: Not once did he raise his voice
outline.gist: His marriage had ordinary problems, and his wives outlived him and told his stories, yet he searched and found no report of him raising his voice, let alone his hand.

outline.heading: Outro

57:4.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ يَعۡلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡهَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعۡرُجُ فِيهَاۖ وَهُوَ مَعَكُمۡ أَيۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرࣱ‏
57:4.en: He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days; then He mounted the Throne. He knoweth all that entereth the earth and all that emergeth therefrom and all that cometh down from the sky and all that ascendeth therein; and He is with you wheresoever ye may be. And Allah is Seer of what ye do

57:5.ar: لَّهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
57:5.en: His is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth, and unto Allah (all) things are brought back

57:6.ar: يُولِجُ ٱلَّيۡلَ فِي ٱلنَّهَارِ وَيُولِجُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فِي ٱلَّيۡلِۚ وَهُوَ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
57:6.en: He causeth the night to pass into the day, and He causeth the day to pass into the night, and He is knower of all that is in the breasts

57:7.ar: ءَامِنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَأَنفِقُواْ مِمَّا جَعَلَكُم مُّسۡتَخۡلَفِينَ فِيهِۖ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَأَنفَقُواْ لَهُمۡ أَجۡرࣱ كَبِيرࣱ‏
57:7.en: Believe in Allah and His messenger, and spend of that whereof He hath made you trustees; and such of you as believe and spend (aright), theirs will be a great reward

57:8.ar: وَمَا لَكُمۡ لَا تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولُ يَدۡعُوكُمۡ لِتُؤۡمِنُواْ بِرَبِّكُمۡ وَقَدۡ أَخَذَ مِيثَٰقَكُمۡ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
57:8.en: What aileth you that ye believe not in Allah, when the messenger calleth you to believe in your Lord, and He hath already made a covenant with you, if ye are believers

57:9.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِهِۦٓ ءَايَٰتِۭ بَيِّنَٰتࣲ لِّيُخۡرِجَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ إِلَى ٱلنُّورِۚ وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِكُمۡ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
57:9.en: He it is Who sendeth down clear revelations unto His slave, that He may bring you forth from darkness unto light; and lo! for you, Allah is Full of Pity, Merciful

57:10.ar: وَمَا لَكُمۡ أَلَّا تُنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِلَّهِ مِيرَٰثُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ لَا يَسۡتَوِي مِنكُم مَّنۡ أَنفَقَ مِن قَبۡلِ ٱلۡفَتۡحِ وَقَٰتَلَۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ أَعۡظَمُ دَرَجَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنفَقُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدُ وَقَٰتَلُواْۚ وَكُلࣰّ ا وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣱ‏
57:10.en: And what aileth you that ye spend not in the way of Allah when unto Allah belongeth the inheritance of the heavens and the earth? Those who spent and fought before the victory are not upon a level (with the rest of you). Such are greater in rank than those who spent and fought afterwards. Unto each hath Allah promised good. And Allah is Informed of what ye do

57:1.ar: سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
57:1.en: All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifieth Allah; and He is the Mighty, the Wise

57:2.ar: لَهُۥ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
57:2.en: His is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth; He quickeneth and He giveth death; and He is Able to do all things

57:3.ar: هُوَ ٱلۡأَوَّلُ وَٱلۡأٓخِرُ وَٱلظَّٰهِرُ وَٱلۡبَاطِنُۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمٌ
57:3.en: He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward; and He is Knower of all things

50:38.ar: وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبࣲ‏
50:38.en: And verily We created the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, in six Days, and naught of weariness touched Us

36:82.ar: إِنَّمَآ أَمۡرُهُۥٓ إِذَآ أَرَادَ شَيۡـًٔا أَن يَقُولَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
36:82.en: But His command, when He intendeth a thing, is only that He saith unto it: Be! and it is

17:67.ar: وَإِذَا مَسَّكُمُ ٱلضُّرُّ فِي ٱلۡبَحۡرِ ضَلَّ مَن تَدۡعُونَ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُۖ فَلَمَّا نَجَّىٰكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡبَرِّ أَعۡرَضۡتُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ كَفُورًا
17:67.en: And when harm toucheth you upon the sea, all unto whom ye cry (for succour) fail save Him (alone), but when He bringeth you safe to land, ye turn away, for man was ever thankless

112:2.en: Allah, the eternally Besought of all

7:172.ar: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ وَأَشۡهَدَهُمۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ أَلَسۡتُ بِرَبِّكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ شَهِدۡنَآۚ أَن تَقُولُواْ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنۡ هَٰذَا غَٰفِلِينَ
7:172.en: And (remember) when thy Lord brought forth from the Children of Adam, from their reins, their seed, and made them testify of themselves, (saying): Am I not your Lord? They said: Yea, verily. We testify. (That was) lest ye should say at the Day of Resurrection: Lo! of this we were unaware

6gKzh7j12EM.speaker: adnan
6gKzh7j12EM.speaker_note: continues his own Sunday tafseer series on Surat al-Hadid from the previous week
6gKzh7j12EM.title: Tafseer of Surat al-Hadid, Part 2: Verses 4-10
6gKzh7j12EM.one_line: Al-Hadid's opening verses describe Allah through apparent opposites to teach that spirituality and material giving must work together.
6gKzh7j12EM.summary: He frames Surat al-Hadid as the close of a cluster of surahs that each set two options before the reader, except that al-Hadid insists on both: spirituality and the material side of faith are not rivals but two ingredients that must be present in the right amounts, and many Muslims feel something missing because one is inflated or absent. He argues that the first six verses describe Allah through pairs that look like opposites, the first and the last, the apparent and the hidden, life and death, and uses tawakkul as an example: full effort and full reliance coexist. Moving through verses 4 to 6, he reads the istawa on the throne figuratively as total command, explains the six days as time that creatures need rather than time Allah needs, and rejects a medieval picture of instant magical creation. Allah being with us wherever we are grounds haya and, above all, comfort in loneliness and despair. Since Allah knows what is in the chests, he urges dropping the social mask in dua and speaking with the humility of sujud. Verse 7 commands belief plus giving from whatever we are stewards of, not just money, and verse 10 shows the same gift weighs differently depending on the spirit behind it.

outline.heading: The cluster of choices and al-Hadid's 'both' answer
outline.gist: Recaps the comparisons running through the preceding surahs; al-Hadid instead says materialism and spirituality are two pieces of one puzzle.

outline.heading: Why Muslims feel something is missing
outline.gist: An imbalance between the two ingredients leaves people inside Islam unable to taste it; mechanics without essence and essence without mechanics both fail.

outline.heading: The first six verses describe Allah through opposites
outline.gist: First and last, apparent and hidden, life and death: what seem to be opposites coexist in Him, a model for holding the spiritual and material together.

outline.heading: Tawakkul after doing your best
outline.gist: Effort and reliance are not alternatives; tawakkul only makes sense after exhausting every resource, while trusting Allah with the outcome you cannot control.

outline.heading: Interlude
Ramadan as the yearly chance to return
outline.gist: However far one has drifted, Ramadan is the annual season to turn things around; intend each year that this Ramadan will be the best.

outline.heading: Interlude
Recap of the attributes so far
outline.gist: Allah as the Exalted, the All-Wise, the sole owner of sovereignty, giver of life and death, beyond time and space.

outline.heading: Rising over the throne as total command
outline.gist: Reads istawa as a figure of speech that nothing runs outside His will, not a literal image of someone seated on a throne.

outline.heading: Why creation took six days
outline.gist: Allah needed no time; creatures do. He cites an interpretation of the six periods as the four seasons plus night and day, without which life could not exist.

outline.heading: Creation over time, not a magic wand
outline.gist: 'Be and it is' means certainty of outcome, not instantaneity; the long, intricate process of life is more awe-inspiring than a medieval image of a God zapping things into existence.

outline.heading: What enters the earth and ascends to the sky
outline.gist: Every seed, burial, rain, decree and deed that moves in or out of the earth and sky is within His knowledge, covering both the material and the spiritual.

outline.heading: He is with you wherever you are: haya
outline.gist: His constant presence by knowledge and mercy is the root of haya and taqwa, and on the Day of Judgment He will be the final witness against denial.

outline.heading: His presence as comfort, not only fear
outline.gist: Teach children they are never alone; in abandonment, pain or even approaching death, Allah's companionship gives peace.

outline.heading: Look out for the lonely
outline.gist: Loneliness is debilitating; make time for isolated people, as the Prophet ensured the lonely had companionship, which is also the wisdom of congregation.

outline.heading: You will cope, even if it does not work out
outline.gist: Knowing Allah is with you does not guarantee the outcome you want, but it lets you endure whatever hand you are dealt.

outline.heading: The ship in the storm and as-Samad
outline.gist: When the sea overwhelms a small ship, everyone instinctively turns to the One all rely on; the question is whether you can turn to Him earlier.

outline.heading: Sovereignty and night merging into day
outline.gist: The repetition of sovereignty now stresses His kingship; the seamless merging of night and day is another pair held together by Him.

outline.heading: He knows what is in the chests
outline.gist: He is aware of every thought, intention and feeling, which is different from holding us accountable for all of it.

outline.heading: Drop the persona when speaking to Allah
outline.gist: We all carry a social persona, but speaking to Allah through it is absurd; real dua is removing the filters and admitting where we truly stand, while vulnerability before people needs great care.

outline.heading: Sujud as the posture of honest need
outline.gist: Placing the most dignified part of the body on the ground should carry a matching inner state; no one speaks formally or as an equal with their face on the floor.

outline.heading: Dua as acknowledgement, and memorizing the six verses
outline.gist: Dua is not Aladdin's lamp but an admission of who you are and who Allah is; he urges memorizing the six verses as a portrait of Allah.

outline.heading: Interlude
Give from what He made you steward of
outline.gist: The verse does not say 'your wealth' but what He entrusted you with as khalifa: money, knowledge, time, expertise, passion or a listening ear.

outline.heading: There is always something to give
outline.gist: Even with nothing, a kind word remains; and the harder life becomes, the more one should give and let Allah sort things out.

outline.heading: Why would you not believe?
outline.gist: The reward for believing and giving, and the challenge of why one would withhold belief while the Messenger calls you.

outline.heading: The primordial covenant and the search for meaning
outline.gist: The covenant taken from humanity sits in the subconscious, which is why every person searches for meaning and purpose; guidance is Allah's generosity.

outline.heading: Clear signs to bring you from darkness to light
outline.gist: Revelation's purpose is extraction from darkness, a gradual transition visible in the companions' lives, driven by Allah's tenderness toward us.

outline.heading: Giving before and after the conquest
outline.gist: The same sum given before the conquest of Makkah outweighs it after, because the spirit and risk behind the act differ: why and how matter alongside what.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Balance of spirituality and material action
themes.note: Al-Hadid requires both the spiritual and the material in the right proportion; inflating or deflating either breaks the practice of Islam.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: The first six verses portray Allah through apparent opposites: first and last, apparent and hidden, creator beyond time, ever-present and all-knowing.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Reliance only means something after full effort; skipping the work and calling it tawakkul misunderstands the equation.

themes.label: Creation, time and science
themes.note: The six days are periods creatures need; creation unfolding over billions of years is more impressive than instant magic and does not diminish 'Be and it is'.

themes.label: Allah's companionship and comfort
themes.note: His presence by knowledge and mercy underlies haya, but its main fruit is comfort in loneliness and the worst moments of life.

themes.label: Caring for the lonely
themes.note: Seek out isolated people and give them time, as the Prophet did; togetherness is part of why we pray in congregation.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: Dua is an honest, unfiltered admission before One who already knows everything, in the humility of sujud, not a wish lamp.

themes.label: Giving from what you are entrusted with
themes.note: Giving covers every trust, not just money; there is always something to give, and the intention and circumstances change its weight.

themes.label: The covenant and the innate search for God
themes.note: The primordial covenant explains the universal human search for meaning and a Lord.

quran.point: Creation of the heavens and earth caused Allah no fatigue, so there was no day of rest.
'Be and it is' signals that His will is certain, not that things happen instantly.
People in a storm at sea turn to Allah alone in helplessness.
As-Samad: the One upon whom all rely and who relies on no one.
The primordial covenant in which humanity acknowledged Allah as Lord.

hadith.gist: The companions described the Prophet settling fully and calmly in each position of prayer, falling into prostration.

maxims: Materialism and spirituality are not opposites
The worse things are for you, the more you give
Tawakkul only exists after you have done your best
Take off the masks and speak to Allah
Dua is not Aladdin's lamp

stories.who: A teacher's father on the six days
stories.point: The six periods are the four seasons plus night and day, the conditions life needs, pointing to creatures' need for time.

stories.who: A small ship in an angry sea
stories.point: In helplessness everyone turns to the Supreme Power; turn to Him before the storm.

stories.who: Two people giving 200 dinars before and after the conquest of Makkah
stories.point: Identical material acts differ in weight because of the faith and risk behind them.

takeaways: Bring both spiritual connection and practical giving into your practice instead of favouring one
Do your full effort before claiming tawakkul
Seek out lonely people around you and give them time
Speak to Allah in dua honestly, without the social persona
Give from whatever you have been entrusted with, even a kind word, and give more when life is hard
